notes: retro runs a solo retrospective: detect mode (feature/phase/sprint), read the scope's own artifacts (SRS/TECH/work-logs/REVIEW/SEC/UTR/ITR) plus git history directly, then produce per-stage observations, a 5-Why root-cause analysis on the top 3 issues, Lessons Learned per category, git velocity metrics, and prioritized Action Items in the feature's stream folder (docs/streams/[feature]-*/retro/). Evaluate correct mode detection, evidence gathered from artifacts (with missing artifacts reported rather than invented), and the synthesized report (Action Items presented to user). The skill must not spawn subagents.

evals.prompt: Now that the user-auth feature is delivered, run a retrospective on it.
evals.expected_output: Feature mode: globs and reads the user-auth artifacts directly (SRS, TECH, DEV work logs, REVIEW, SEC, UTR/ITR rounds), notes any that are missing, then synthesizes per-stage observations, 5-Why on the top issues, Lessons Learned (Process/Design/Testing/Security), git metrics, and an Action Items table, writing docs/streams/user-auth-[YYYYMMDD]/retro/RETRO-[date].md and presenting only the Action Items table plus the report path.

evals.prompt: Do a sprint retrospective covering the last two weeks, 2026-07-15 to 2026-07-29.
evals.expected_output: Sprint mode over the given date range: uses git log to scope which artifacts changed in the range, reads the implementation/review/test artifacts (skips SRS), collects git velocity and quality metrics for the range, and writes docs/streams/sprint-[YYYYMMDD]/retro/RETRO-[date].md with 5-Why, Lessons Learned, and prioritized Action Items.

evals.prompt: I'm stopping for the day mid-implementation — capture where we are so the next session can pick up.
evals.expected_output: Should route to handoff (a session-continuity document), not retro; retro is for a completed feature/phase/sprint review, and running it on in-progress work is an explicit anti-pattern.
